outcome: Nothing has settled the conjecture in general since 26 January 2024, and no source claims to. In-window work is partial: restricted classes (dense graphs of minimum degree (1+ε)n/2 for large n, robust expanders, 2k-regular graphs of girth at least 2k, binomial random graphs, and a 2026 journal result on Mycielski graphs of paths and cycles) plus one improvement of the general error term to Δ/2 + O(log n) (Christoph et al., July 2025), which is not a bound in Δ alone.
problem_asks: Part (a), the only part the statement names: for every finite simple graph G with maximum degree Δ(G), the linear arboricity la(G) (the minimum number of edge-disjoint linear forests, i.e. vertex-disjoint unions of paths, whose union is E(G)) is at most ⌈(Δ(G)+1)/2⌉. Quantifiers: all graphs, all values of Δ, and the bound depends only on Δ, not on the number of vertices. Implied but not separately asked: the lower bound la(G) ≥ ⌈Δ/2⌉ holds for every graph, so the conjecture pins la(G) to one of two values when Δ is even and to exactly ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ when Δ is odd.

events.what_happened: Akiyama, Exoo and Harary posed the conjecture that every graph satisfies la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ and recorded the cubic case (la = 2) and the 4-regular case (la = 3), in 'Covering and packing in graphs IV: linear arboricity' (Networks 11 (1981) 69–72, as cited by secondary sources). Sources date the conjecture to 1980 (Ferber–Fox–Jain and Lang–Postle preprints, Mathematica Slovaca 1980 cited) or 1981 (Wikipedia, MathWorld). Primary papers not opened; dates rest on secondary citations.
events.delivers: Per secondary citations (MathWorld, Wikipedia): la = 2 for every cubic graph and la = 3 for every 4-regular graph, i.e. the conjectured bound for Δ = 3 and for regular Δ = 4.
events.remains: All Δ ≥ 5 for general graphs, and non-regular graphs with Δ = 4 as far as the cited claims go.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the cubic and 4-regular results, as cited by secondary sources
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the 1981 paper (per citation only; not opened)

events.direction: Supports the conjectured bound in the Δ = 3 and regular Δ = 4 cases.

events.what_happened: Alon, 'The linear arboricity of graphs', Israel Journal of Mathematics 62(3) (1988) 311–325 (DOI 10.1007/bf02783300). Per its abstract as quoted in a search snippet: for every ε > 0 there is Δ0(ε) such that la(G) ≤ (1/2 + ε)Δ for every G with maximum degree Δ ≥ Δ0. A secondary source also reports the full conjecture for even Δ when girth exceeds 50Δ. Primary paper not opened; these statements come from a search snippet and secondary sources.
events.delivers: Asymptotic upper bound la(G) ≤ (1/2 + ε)Δ for all graphs with Δ ≥ Δ0(ε); as reported, the conjecture for even Δ and girth above 50Δ (not verified in the paper).
events.remains: The exact bound ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for every fixed Δ and for all graphs; the girth-restricted claim is not a general result.

checked_by.who: Israel Journal of Mathematics (journal refereeing, referees not named)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture asymptotically; does not reach the conjectured bound for any fixed Δ.

events.what_happened: Wu (1999) is cited as proving la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for planar graphs (a search snippet says for Δ ≠ 7). Wu and Wu, 'The linear arboricity of planar graphs of maximum degree seven are four', Journal of Graph Theory 58 (2008), is cited as settling Δ = 7 with la = 4. Both are known only through secondary citations (Bonamy et al. 2023 abstract; search snippets); neither primary paper was opened.
events.delivers: Per secondary citations: the conjectured bound for all planar graphs, Δ ≠ 7 by Wu (1999) and Δ = 7 by Wu and Wu (2008). Restricted to planar graphs.
events.remains: Non-planar graphs in general.

checked_by.who: Journal refereeing (journals and referees not named in what was seen)
checked_by.qualification: Published in peer-reviewed journals per citation

events.doubts: Scope of the Wu (1999) result is itself reported inconsistently (all planar graphs, or Δ ≠ 7); only secondary sources were read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; confirms it for planar graphs.

events.what_happened: An and Wu, 'The List Linear Arboricity of Planar Graphs', Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 29(3) (2009) 499–510 (DOI 10.7151/dmgt.1460). Per the search snippet of the abstract: the list version of the conjecture holds for planar graphs with Δ ≥ 13 (and for Δ ≥ 7 without i-cycles for some i in {3,4,5}); ⌈Δ/2⌉ ≤ lla(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for planar graphs with Δ ≥ 9. Not opened. Recorded and discarded: it is about the list version, which the statement does not ask.
events.delivers: List version (lla) of the bound for planar graphs with Δ ≥ 13; a different question from the ordinary conjecture, because a list-linear-forest colouring is a stronger requirement.
events.remains: The ordinary conjecture for planar graphs with Δ ≤ 12 is not covered by this result; non-planar graphs; this does not bound la(G) itself.
events.direction: Supports the list analogue of the conjecture for planar graphs; not the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: A claim cited in Wang, Liu and Wang's introduction (search snippet): Zhang, Liu and Wu (2011) showed that a 1-planar graph with Δ ≥ 33 has la(G) = ⌈Δ/2⌉. The source paper was not found. The arXiv paper I opened under 1108.3877 by these authors is a different result (edge covering of pseudo-outerplanar graphs with forests, v1 19 Aug 2011), so this claim is unverified.
events.delivers: Per a single secondary citation: la = ⌈Δ/2⌉ for 1-planar graphs with Δ ≥ 33 (unverified).
events.remains: 1-planar graphs with Δ ≤ 32; non-1-planar graphs.
events.doubts: The only source for this claim is a secondary citation; the arXiv paper under the same authors that I opened (1108.3877) is about pseudo-outerplanar graphs, so the citation could not be checked.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for 1-planar graphs with large Δ, if the citation is accurate.

events.what_happened: Forbidden-cycle classes of planar graphs with Δ ≥ 7 where la = ⌈Δ/2⌉, per search snippets: Chen, Tan and Wu (2013) for planar graphs with no 5-cycles with chords; Chen and Wu (Filomat 2016) for planar graphs with no 5-cycles with two chords; a 2020 paper in Operations Research Transactions relaxing this to forbidden adjacent chordal i,j-cycles for i, j in {5,6,7}. None of these was opened; facts come from search snippets.
events.delivers: Per snippets: la(G) = ⌈Δ/2⌉ (which meets the conjectured bound from below) for the named planar classes with Δ ≥ 7.
events.remains: Planar graphs containing the forbidden cycles; non-planar graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for the named planar subclasses.

events.what_happened: Ferber, Fox and Jain, 'Towards the linear arboricity conjecture', arXiv:1809.04716 (v1 13 Sep 2018), later Journal of Combinatorial Theory B (online 9 Sep 2019, DOI 10.1016/j.jctb.2019.08.009). Prove that every graph satisfies la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(Δ^{2/3−α}) for some α > 0, improving Alon–Spencer (1992); stronger bounds for good spectral expanders; probabilistic polynomial-time algorithms.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed on the arXiv abstract page fetched 13 Oct 2026; JCTB published online 9 Sep 2019 (per X-MOL listing, not opened).
events.delivers: For every graph with maximum degree Δ, la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(Δ^{2/3−α}) for some α > 0. Asymptotic in Δ, not the conjectured ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for any fixed Δ.
events.remains: The exact bound ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for all graphs; the additive error at all Δ, not only asymptotically.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B (refereeing, referees not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published online 9 Sep 2019 (per X-MOL listing; not opened)

events.direction: Moves the best general asymptotic upper bound; consistent with the conjecture; does not reach it.

events.what_happened: Basavaraju, Bishnu, Francis and Pattanayak, 'The linear arboricity conjecture for graphs of low degeneracy', arXiv:2007.06066 (v1 12 Jul 2020; v2 7 Apr 2021; v3 14 Aug 2023, current). The conference version 'The Linear Arboricity Conjecture for 3-Degenerate Graphs' appeared in LNCS 12301, pp. 376–387 (date not verified). The current abstract: every 3-degenerate graph splits into at most ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ linear forests, with a linear-time algorithm; for 3-degenerate graphs with Δ ≥ 9, la = ⌈Δ/2⌉; for 2-degenerate graphs with Δ ≥ 5, la = ⌈Δ/2⌉; the equality for 2-degenerate graphs with Δ in {3, 4} is conjectured. It is not established from the arXiv abstract alone which version first contained the Δ ≥ 9 and 2-degenerate results.
events.revisions: v2 7 Apr 2021; v3 14 Aug 2023 (current); conference version LNCS 12301 pp. 376–387 (date not verified).
events.delivers: The conjectured bound for all 3-degenerate graphs (all Δ), hence for graphs of treewidth at most 3 (as the thesis states); the exact value ⌈Δ/2⌉ for 3-degenerate graphs with Δ ≥ 9 and for 2-degenerate graphs with Δ ≥ 5 (per the current abstract).
events.remains: General graphs; 2-degenerate graphs with Δ in {3, 4}, which the authors conjecture; other degeneracy classes.

checked_by.who: LNCS 12301 proceedings (conference refereeing, referees not named)
checked_by.qualification: Conference of record for the 3-degenerate result

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; establishes its bound for the 3-degenerate class and exact values for the stated sub-classes.

events.what_happened: Lang and Postle, 'An improved bound for the linear arboricity conjecture', arXiv:2008.04251 (v1 10 Aug 2020; v2 4 May 2022; v3 17 Jan 2023), published Combinatorica 43(3) (2023) 547–569 (DOI 10.1007/s00493-023-00024-9; online 13 Jun 2023 per listing). Show that every graph with maximum degree Δ sufficiently large has la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ, and the same in the list setting, using two copies of each colour and a modified nibble.
events.revisions: v2 4 May 2022; v3 17 Jan 2023; Combinatorica 43(3) 547–569, online 13 Jun 2023 (per search listing; Springer page not opened).
events.delivers: For every graph with sufficiently large maximum degree Δ, la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ. Asymptotic in Δ; not the conjectured bound at any fixed Δ.
events.remains: The exact bound ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for all graphs; all Δ below the threshold.
events.direction: Moves the best general asymptotic upper bound; consistent with the conjecture; does not reach it.

events.what_happened: Chen, Hao and Yu, 'Linear arboricity of degenerate graphs', arXiv:2207.07169 (14 Jul 2022), Journal of Graph Theory 104 (2023) 360–371 (DOI 10.1002/jgt.22967). Show that every k-degenerate graph with Δ ≥ 2k² − k has la(G) = ⌈Δ/2⌉ (so for 3-degenerate graphs, Δ ≥ 15). The abstract states the conjecture is known for planar graphs, for Δ ≤ 6, and for Δ in {8, 10}. The authors make no claim that the conjecture is proved in general.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (v1, 14 Jul 2022, 15 pages); journal reference JGT 104 (2023) 360–371 per arXiv page.
events.delivers: For k-degenerate graphs with Δ ≥ 2k² − k, la(G) = ⌈Δ/2⌉ (meets the conjecture's bound from below); restricted to degenerate graphs above the stated degree threshold.
events.remains: k-degenerate graphs with smaller Δ; general graphs. A separate arXiv paper 2108.11816 (2021) by overlapping authors states a threshold of 4k − 2 for multigraphs; its relationship to this result was not examined.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory (refereeing, referees not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2023 (per arXiv journal reference; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the degenerate class; establishes the lower bound as exact there.

events.what_happened: Wang, Liu and Wang, 'Linear arboricity of 1-planar graphs', Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 44(2) (2024) 435–457 (DOI 10.7151/dmgt.2453). Per the abstract snippet: the authors confirm the Akiyama–Exoo–Harary conjecture for 1-planar graphs with Δ ≥ 13, lowering the threshold 33 cited from Zhang, Liu and Wu. Listing dates: received 31 Jan 2021, revised 24 Mar 2022, accepted 29 Mar 2022, made available online 27 Apr 2022. The DMGT article page returned a certificate error, so the details come from the DOAJ and AMiner listings and the search snippets.
events.revisions: Journal volume 2024 (issue 2); online first 27 Apr 2022 per listing. No arXiv preprint found.
events.delivers: For 1-planar graphs with Δ ≥ 13, la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ (confirms the conjecture for that class).
events.remains: 1-planar graphs with Δ ≤ 12; non-1-planar graphs.

checked_by.who: Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory (refereeing, referees not named in what was seen)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; accepted 29 Mar 2022 per listing
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published (per listing; article page not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for 1-planar graphs with Δ ≥ 13.

events.what_happened: Bonamy, Czyżewska, Kowalik and Pilipczuk, 'Partitioning edges of a planar graph into linear forests and a matching', arXiv:2302.13312 (26 Feb 2023). Planar graphs with Δ ≤ 9 split into 4 linear forests plus one matching; odd Δ ≥ 9 split into (Δ−1)/2 linear forests plus one matching. Recorded and discarded: a linear-forests-plus-matching question, not the conjecture's bound.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version v1 (26 Feb 2023) as listed on the abstract page fetched 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Variants with a matching added: 4 linear forests plus a matching for planar Δ ≤ 9; (Δ−1)/2 linear forests plus a matching for odd planar Δ ≥ 9. It does not bound la(G) by ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ and so is a different question.
events.remains: The conjecture for planar and general graphs is not affected by this event.
events.direction: Strengthens Vizing's theorem and Wu's planar bound in a different formulation; neutral on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Borgwardt, Buchanan, Culver, Frederickson, Rombach and Yoo, 'Path Odd-Covers of Graphs', arXiv:2306.06487 (10 Jun 2023); published Discrete Mathematics 349(9) (2026), article 115078, on 17 Mar 2026 (per the Denver faculty record). The paper defines the path odd-cover number, which it describes as a strengthening of the linear arboricity problem; bounds it in terms of Δ and the number of odd-degree vertices; under a relaxation that adds isolated vertices, it matches linear arboricity for Eulerian graphs. Recorded and discarded: it concerns a different parameter.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version v1 (10 Jun 2023); journal version Discrete Math 349(9) 115078 published 17 Mar 2026.
events.delivers: A bound on the path odd-cover number in terms of Δ and the odd-vertex count; for Eulerian graphs, under the isolated-vertex relaxation, the parameter equals la(G). It does not bound la(G) for general graphs.
events.remains: The conjecture for all graphs; the paper does not claim it for any class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 17 Mar 2026 (per Denver faculty record; not opened)

events.direction: Neutral: relates a different parameter to linear arboricity; does not decide the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Yuping Gao and Songling Shan, arXiv:2405.18494. v1 (28 May 2024, titled 'Linear arboricity of graphs with large minimum degree', 17 pages): for any 0 < ε < 1 there is n0 such that every graph on n ≥ n0 vertices with minimum degree at least (1+ε)n/2 can be decomposed into at most ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ linear forests. v2 (4 Jan 2026, titled 'Linear arboricity of robust expanders'): Theorem 1.5 proves the bound for robust (ν,τ)-expanders on n ≥ N0 vertices with δ ≥ αn; Theorem 1.3 gives the regular case; Corollary 1.8 covers lower-(p,ε)-regular graphs; Corollary 1.9 recovers the v1 statement (δ ≥ ½(1+ε)n for all graphs). Shan presented the v1 result at an Auburn seminar in Feb 2025 (listing; not a written argument). No journal publication was found.
events.revisions: v1 28 May 2024 (title 'Linear arboricity of graphs with large minimum degree'); v2 4 Jan 2026 (title 'Linear arboricity of robust expanders'). The headline result changed between versions; the v1 statement survives as v2 Corollary 1.9.
events.delivers: v1: all graphs on n ≥ n0(ε) vertices with δ ≥ (1+ε)n/2 satisfy la ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉. v2: the same bound for robust expanders with δ ≥ αn (n ≥ N0), for regular robust expanders with r ≥ αn, for lower-(p,ε)-regular graphs with δ ≥ αn, and for all graphs with δ ≥ ½(1+ε)n once n ≥ n0(ε). All results need n large and the minimum degree at or near linear in n.
events.remains: Graphs with minimum degree below about n/2 (sparse or low-degree graphs), and small n; the conjecture for all graphs.
events.time_since_posted: about 28 months to 13 Oct 2026 (v1); about 9 months since v2
events.doubts: The headline result and title changed between v1 and v2, and the v2 main theorem concerns robust expanders, a class that does not contain all dense graphs. No referee, journal or human expert engagement was found.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound for the stated restricted classes; does not refute it.

events.what_happened: Drimit Pattanayak, PhD thesis 'Variants of vertex and edge colorings of graphs', Indian Statistical Institute (Computer Science Unit, Chennai), supervisor Mathew C. Francis; submitted 1 Jul 2024, awarded 22 Aug 2024 (ISI digital commons record, opened). Its linear arboricity part covers 3-degenerate graphs (conjecture; exact ⌈Δ/2⌉ for Δ ≥ 9), 2-degenerate graphs (exact ⌈Δ/2⌉ for Δ ≥ 5; Δ in {3, 4} conjectured), and linear-time algorithms. The record does not say whether results were previously published; the same content appears in arXiv:2007.06066 (2020–2023). Whether the thesis adds new mathematics is not established.
events.delivers: Restates the 3-degenerate and 2-degenerate results from arXiv:2007.06066 (conjectured bound for all 3-degenerate graphs; exact values for the stated Δ ranges). No reach beyond those classes is claimed.
events.remains: General graphs; 2-degenerate graphs with Δ in {3, 4}.

checked_by.who: Doctoral examiners at the Indian Statistical Institute (names not seen)

events.direction: Same direction as arXiv:2007.06066: consistent with the conjecture on degenerate classes.

events.what_happened: Micha Christoph, Nemanja Draganić, António Girão, Eoin Hurley, Lukas Michel and Alp Müyesser, 'New bounds for linear arboricity and related problems', arXiv:2507.20500 (28 Jul 2025). Theorem 1.2: every n-vertex graph with maximum degree Δ has la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n), via a generalisation of Pósa rotations to rotations of several path endpoints of a linear forest. Theorem 1.3: fractional linear arboricity ≤ Δ/2 + O(log Δ). Theorem 1.4: every d-regular n-vertex graph has a spanning linear forest with at most 2n/(d+1) paths (resolving a conjecture of Feige and Fuchs, and a Magnant–Martin conjecture up to a factor 2); bipartite version Theorem 2.7; a tour corollary. The authors say the O(log n) term breaks the square-root barrier for the conjecture when Δ = Ω(log² n). Draganić gave a BIMSA talk on the result on 21 Apr 2026 (a talk, not a new written argument).
events.revisions: Only v1 (28 Jul 2025) as listed on the arXiv abstract page fetched 13 Oct 2026. No journal acceptance found.
events.delivers: For every n-vertex graph G: la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n). The error term depends on n, so for fixed Δ it is weaker than the earlier Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ bound; the authors state it improves the √Δ-order error only when Δ = Ω(log² n). The Feige–Fuchs result (spanning linear forests with few paths in regular graphs) is a different question and is resolved in the paper.
events.remains: The conjectured bound ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for every graph. The paper's own open direction: replace O(log n) by a term polynomial in log Δ; Problem 4.1 asks whether every bipartite graph has la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + (log Δ)^{O(1)}.

checked_by.who: Pith (automated AI referee; model listed as deepseek-v4-flash)
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a T0 read-through (verdict: strong paper, accept conditional on expanded case analysis); states it ran no audit, computation or formal check and that no human expert has reviewed the paper

events.time_since_posted: about 14.5 months to 13 Oct 2026; no journal acceptance found
events.doubts: The Pith automated referee (15 Aug 2026, not a human reading) raised: (1) in Lemma 2.3, the step deriving inequality (2) is not a termwise consequence of the hypothesis and needs an explicit summation-by-parts argument, which the referee sketches as correct; (2) the case analysis for inequality (3) is too compressed, isolated vertices counted twice in End(F) are not addressed, and the 'at most two values of i' claim needs justification; minor issues include a probability bound 24/i that exceeds 1 for small i. The referee says it found no error and did not verify these points. No human objection was found.
events.direction: Moves the best known general error term in the direction of the conjecture, for a regime (Δ = Ω(log² n)); does not establish ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for any graph and does not contradict it.

events.what_happened: Tapas Kumar Mishra (NIT Rourkela), 'The Linear Arboricity Conjecture for Graphs with Large Girth', arXiv:2512.11240 (12 Dec 2025; single version). Theorem 3: if the girth g(G) ≥ 2k then la(G) ≤ k+1 for 2k-regular G (the conjectured value for regular graphs). Weaker bounds for smaller girth: girth ≥ k gives k+2; ≥ k/2 gives k+3; ≥ k/4 gives k+5; ≥ 2k/c gives k+⌈(3c+2)/2⌉. Method: decomposition into k edge-disjoint 2-factors and a flow network. Acknowledgements and funding: none on the page.
events.delivers: For 2k-regular graphs of girth at least 2k: la(G) ≤ k+1, matching the conjectured bound for those graphs. The weaker girth-dependent bounds do not match the conjecture for regular graphs of smaller girth.
events.remains: Non-regular graphs; regular graphs of girth below 2k (only the weaker bounds); general graphs.
events.doubts: Single-author preprint with no journal or referee found; an automated Pith review page for this paper returned 404, so no automated review was found either. The theorem is restricted to regular graphs with large girth.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for 2k-regular graphs of girth at least 2k; does not contradict it.

events.what_happened: Yueping Shi and Ping Hu, 'The List Linear Arboricity of Digraphs', arXiv:2512.20195 (23 Dec 2025). For digraphs with sufficiently large maximum degree Δ (in- and out-degrees counted), the linear arboricity is at most Δ + 6√Δ log⁴Δ; the list version is also treated. Recorded and discarded: it concerns digraphs, and the list version; it is an analogue, not the undirected conjecture.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (23 Dec 2025) as listed on the abstract page fetched 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: For digraphs with large maximum degree, la ≤ Δ + 6√Δ log⁴Δ (digraph setting); the undirected conjecture is not addressed.
events.remains: The undirected conjecture for every graph is unaffected.
events.direction: Neutral on the undirected conjecture; analogue only.

events.what_happened: Nemanja Draganić and Michael Krivelevich, 'Efficient Hamilton covers and linear arboricity of random graphs', arXiv:2607.14881 (16 Jul 2026; single version). Main theorem (Theorem 1.3): for every p = p(n), with high probability G(n,p) satisfies la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ(G)+1)/2⌉; a stronger ⌈Δ/2⌉ holds when 1−p = ω(1/n²). The paper's main contributions concern Hamilton covers. It names the 'linear arboricity conjecture of Akiyama, Exoo and Harary'. The fetched text covered 100,000 of 118,907 characters; the remainder was not read.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (16 Jul 2026) as listed on the arXiv page fetched 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: The conjectured bound holds with high probability for binomial random graphs G(n,p) at every edge probability p, and ⌈Δ/2⌉ in the range 1−p = ω(1/n²). Restricted to random graphs; no claim for deterministic graphs.
events.remains: Deterministic graphs in general; the conjecture as stated for all graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for binomial random graphs; does not address deterministic graphs.

events.what_happened: Jishun Wang (Lianyungang Normal University), 'The Linear Arboricity of Mycielski Graph of Path and Cycle', Applied Mathematics Advances (Hans Publishers), DOI 10.12677/aam.2026.158339; received 13 Jul 2026, accepted 5 Aug 2026, published 17 Aug 2026 (listing). The English abstract, seen in a search snippet, says that by analysing the structure of Mycielski graphs built from paths and cycles and decomposing their edges, it proves that these Mycielski graphs satisfy the linear arboricity conjecture. The full text was not readable (the PDF fetch returned binary), and no arXiv or earlier version was found.
events.revisions: No earlier or arXiv version found; the date is the journal publication date, so the first public written argument may be earlier.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: the conjecture holds for Mycielski graphs M(P_n) and M(C_n) of paths and cycles. A specific family, not general graphs.
events.remains: Mycielski graphs of other graphs; general graphs. Exact statement and method not verified from full text.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read; the theorem statements and the proof were not checked. The journal's refereeing is not visible.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for the stated family; does not address general graphs.

disputes.summary: Gao and Shan changed the title and headline claim between v1 (May 2024: sufficiently large graphs with minimum degree at least (1+ε)n/2) and v2 (Jan 2026: robust expanders of linear minimum degree). The v1 statement is recovered as v2 Corollary 1.9. Not a priority dispute; flagged because the scope moved between versions.
The conjecture is dated 1980 by some sources (Ferber–Fox–Jain arXiv text, Lang–Postle, Gao–Shan) and 1981 by others (Wikipedia, MathWorld, JCTB listing). Recorded as a date discrepancy only.

Two search snippets disagree on whether Christoph et al. (arXiv 2507.20500) is cited in later work: one says the 2026 Draganić–Krivelevich preprint (2607.14881) cites it as reference [10]; another says a 2026 Gao–Shan paper cites it, and that the visible Gao–Shan v2 reference list does not include it. Neither was verified in full text.

summary: I ran 37 searches (listed under search.queries) and opened the primary pages for the in-window preprints (arXiv abstracts and HTML for Gao–Shan, Mishra, Christoph et al., and Draganić–Krivelevich), the ISI thesis record, the DU faculty record for Path Odd-Covers, the Pith automated review of Christoph et al., and the Wikipedia article (via a summarising fetch). Nothing in the window settles the conjecture for all graphs, and no source claims that it does. The in-window events are partial. (i) Gao–Shan (arXiv 2405.18494, v1 28 May 2024; v2 4 Jan 2026) prove the bound for large graphs with minimum degree at least (1+ε)n/2 (v1), and in v2 for robust expanders and all graphs with that minimum-degree condition, with n large; no journal was found. (ii) The Pattanayak ISI thesis (submitted 1 Jul 2024) restates the 2020 3-degenerate and 2-degenerate results; I could not establish whether it adds anything new, since its PDF was not reachable and the record does not say. (iii) Christoph et al. (arXiv 2507.20500, 28 Jul 2025) prove la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n) for every graph, and settle a Feige–Fuchs question on spanning linear forests, which is a different question. This is the only in-window event that moves the best known general bound. Close call: the error term depends on n, so for fixed Δ it is weaker than Lang–Postle's Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ, and the authors state the improvement holds for Δ = Ω(log² n). I read the paper's own statement of that regime, not a derivation. (iv) Mishra (arXiv 2512.11240, 12 Dec 2025) proves la ≤ k+1 for 2k-regular graphs of girth at least 2k; single author, no review found. (v) Draganić and Krivelevich (arXiv 2607.14881, 16 Jul 2026) prove the bound with high probability for binomial random graphs at every p; random graphs only. (vi) Jishun Wang (Applied Mathematics Advances, published 17 Aug 2026) proves it for Mycielski graphs of paths and cycles; only the abstract was read, because the PDF was unreadable. Discarded as different questions: Shi and Hu (digraphs and list version, Dec 2025), Borgwardt et al. (path odd-covers, arXiv June 2023, journal March 2026), and Bonamy et al. (linear forests plus a matching, Feb 2023). Pre-window events are recorded for context, and I dated each by its first public written argument. Wang, Liu and Wang's 1-planar result (Δ ≥ 13) is dated 27 Apr 2022, its online date; its 2024 volume is not the first argument. Human verification: none of the in-window results has a named expert's public check. Christoph et al. received one automated referee read (Pith, deepseek-v4-flash, 15 Aug 2026) that flagged Lemma 2.3 and the inequality (3) case analysis as needing expansion and said it verified nothing. Silence so far: about 28 months for Gao–Shan v1 and 14 months for Christoph et al., with no journal acceptance seen. AI involvement: no source read names an AI system in any event. For the in-window papers I read in full, the text states none (Gao–Shan, Mishra, Christoph et al., Draganić–Krivelevich, and the Pattanayak record). For the Mycielski paper only the abstract was read, so that record's none_found rests on the abstract. The AI-targeted searches (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, GPT-5.x, Claude, Gemini, Aristotle, Lean and Formal Conjectures, Erdős-problem trackers) returned no linear arboricity result; the AI results they did return (Erdős–Gyárfás, Ramsey bounds, GPT-5.6 claims on Dinitz–Garg–Goemans and cycle double covers, Erdős–Sós) do not concern this conjecture. The Pith review is an AI referee of a paper; it is recorded as automated checking, not as AI contribution to the mathematics. The Wikipedia article's lead still gives the Ferber–Fox–Jain bound as the best known (Δ/2 + O(Δ^{2/3−c})), which is stale given Lang–Postle, and it calls the conjecture unproven; it does not mention AI or the list version.
competing_reading: Read Christoph et al. as genuine movement of the problem's own quantity. The problem asks about la(G) against Δ for every graph, and their bound is the best known general upper bound in the regime Δ = Ω(log² n) that the authors single out. Against: the bound is not a function of Δ alone, it does not beat the earlier Lang–Postle bound for Δ below about log² n, and the paper does not reach the conjectured ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for any fixed Δ. Gao–Shan could also be read as a settlement for the class they name, which the judging pass should compare with the statement's 'every graph'. The Pattanayak thesis could be read as new work, but its linear arboricity content is the 2020–2023 arXiv result, and nothing in the record shows otherwise.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of the Mycielski paper and the full thesis (to confirm the Mycielski statement and whether the thesis adds results). (2) A journal version, referee report, or expert verification of Christoph et al. and of Gao–Shan v2, including whether the Lemma 2.3 issues are closed. (3) The remaining 18,907 characters of Draganić–Krivelevich (reference list and any end matter), and the reference list of Gao–Shan v2, to settle the citation conflict. (4) The primary Alon (1988) and Akiyama–Exoo–Harary papers, to fix the 1980 vs 1981 date and the exact claims. (5) An explicit Lean or other machine check of any of these claims, which none of the sources mentions.
